title: Power Platform: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer carry before-and-after values
summary: The removal of field values, the published dates and both Dataverse control rows are supported. Hold the briefing because its checklist treats environment auditing as sufficient to send events to Purview, although Microsoft requires additional configuration. The licensing model also understates the published licensing for the surrounding service.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse audit events sent to Purview no longer include before-and-after field change values.
claims.quote: Starting in May 2026, Dataverse will no longer include before-and-after field change values in the audit events that are sent to Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Create and update events, including before-and-after column values, remain captured in Dataverse audit logs.
claims.quote: In Dataverse audit logs, create and update events—including a column’s before-and-after values—are captured. These values remain in Dataverse audit logs, but aren’t sent to Purview activity logging.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes preventing leaks of financial, medical, health and personally identifiable customer information as the aim.
claims.quote: To help prevent leaking sensitive customer data from Dataverse audit logs, all customer data is removed before these audit events are sent to Purview activity logging. Examples of sensitive customer data include financial information, medical and health data, and personally identifiable information.

claims.claim: Audit events continue to flow to Purview.
claims.quote: Audit events will continue to flow to Purview; however, the detailed field-level value changes will be excluded.

claims.claim: Purview continues receiving metadata identifying who made changes.
claims.quote: Purview continues receiving audit event metadata (such as who made changes, the date of the changes, and the tables affected), but field-level value changes will no longer be included.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Monitoring, alerting and reporting solutions depending on before-and-after values within Purview events stop working when the change takes effect.
claims.quote: If you have existing monitoring, alerting, or reporting solutions that depend on before-and-after field change values within Purview audit events, those solutions will stop working once this deprecation takes effect.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is controlled in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings > Global Audit Settings > Start Auditing.
claims.quote: Select Manage in the navigation pane. In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment. Select Settings. Expand Audit and logs and then select Audit settings. ... Select Global Audit Settings ... turn on Start Auditing

claims.claim: PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) sets environment auditing through the isauditenabled request-body property.
claims.quote: isauditenabled ... Whether auditing is enabled for the environment ... Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment. ... PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID]) HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: A System Administrator or System Customizer role, or equivalent permissions, is required to change auditing settings.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Dataverse and model-driven app user access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.
claims.quote: User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.claim: The model-driven app route to Audit Summary is Settings > Advanced Settings > System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.
claims.quote: From the app, select the Settings icon on the banner, select Advanced Settings, and then select System > Auditing > Audit Summary view.

claims.quote: To use these messages, ensure you have the prvReadRecordAuditHistory and prvReadAuditSummary privileges.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence or meter specific to the removal of before-and-after values.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse Purview removal before after field values default opt out licensing meter licence Power Platform auditing'; opened the removal notice, activity logs overview and Microsoft Purview service description. No removal-specific licence or meter was stated.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown, with notes limiting the gap to this change and acknowledging surrounding licensing conditions.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E3/A3/A1/G3/F3/F1 | Office 365 E3/E1/A3/A1/G3/G1/F3 | Microsoft 365 Business Basic/Standard/Premium |
| Audit (Standard) | Included | Included | Included |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Add to licensing.notes: 'Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) is included in the plans listed in the Microsoft Purview service description, including Microsoft 365 E3 and Office 365 E3; no licence or meter specific to this removal is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The option to turn on audit logging is visible only when minimum Office licensing requirements are met.
claims.quote: The option to turn on audit logging is only visible when the minimum Office licensing requirements are met.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: Production environments with auditing turned on in Audit settings are the environments whose events reach Purview.
claims.quote: A Power Platform system admin or customizer needs to configure auditing in the Power Platform admin center and then turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting for each Power Platform production environment so Microsoft Purview auditing solutions can access the environment's activity logs.
claims.fix: Replace the checklist bullet with: 'Confirm which production environments have auditing turned on in Audit settings (controls table, row 1).' Remove the clause 'since those are the environments whose events reach Purview': auditing alone does not establish that Purview receives their events.

claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy and Security > Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings > Enable SAS Logging in Purview.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... Select Environments ... Select the production environment ... Select Settings ... Expand the Product list and select Privacy and Security. In the Storage Shared Access Signature (SAS) Security Settings section, toggle the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting to On.

claims.claim: Enable SAS Logging in Purview gives Purview access to activity logs for each configured production environment.
claims.quote: To give Microsoft Purview access to Power Platform environment data, turn on the Enable SAS Logging in Purview setting in the Power Platform admin center for each Power Platform production environment where you want to view audit logs in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The notice documents no opt-in, opt-out or step restoring removed values to Purview; the existing controls enable auditing or read Dataverse data instead.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Dataverse" "before-and-after" "Purview" "opt" "restore"'; read the removal notice, Manage Dataverse auditing, Configure auditing, Retrieve the history of audited data changes and activity logs overview. No removal toggle or restoration step was documented.
